newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northeast spot power steady amid mild weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northeast spot power steady amid mild weather.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the northeastern U.S. finished steady Tuesday amid seasonal temperatures in the region.
"The load is flat. It's normal weather for November," said a New York trader.

The relatively mild temperatures overrode slightly reduced power supplies from Hydro-Quebec. The Canadian utility today scaled back power supplied to the New York Power Authority while it worked on a transformer along one of its two export lines to New York.
Hydro-Quebec today said it expected the high-voltage line to resume normal transmission Wednesday.
In the western part of the New York Power Pool (NYPP) district, peak, non-firm electricity for Wednesday was again quoted at $22.00-$24.00 a megawatt hour (MWh).
Western NYPP power for non-firm delivery during light load hours on Wednesday remained steady $14.00.
In the eastern part of NYPP, peak, non-firm electricity for Wednesday was held steady in the $28.00-$29.00 range, with bids heard as low as $26.00.
Off-peak, non-firm Wednesday electricity in eastern NYPP was pegged at $17.00-$18.00, flat from Monday.
In the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), peak, non-firm electricity for Wednesday at the Northeast Utilities border was assessed at $33.00-$34.00, a much narrower range than Monday's $29.00-$35.00.
Non-firm, off-peak NEPOOL power for Wednesday delivery to the NU border was offered at $23.00-$24.00, compared with a Monday quote near $20.00.
The 619 megawatt (MW) oil-fired Wyman 4 generating unit in Yarmouth, Maine, was scheduled to resume operation today after being shut October 5 for seasonal maintenance.
For Wednesday, temperatures in the northeastern corner of the country were predicted to hit 30s-40s Fahrenheit during the day and 20s-30s at night.
Extended outlook showed the region would experience colder-than-normal weather next week.
